slot.subtopic: Mean free path / mean free time
slot.brief: Hard statement-evaluation MCQ mixing gas laws and kinetic theory: assess which statements about rms speed, mean free path, degrees of freedom and pressure of an ideal gas are true, including a non-obvious one (e.g. mean free path independent of temperature at constant pressure).

stem: Consider an ideal gas of fixed molecular diameter; for the diatomic gas mentioned below, vibrational modes are inactive. Which statements are true? I. At constant pressure, mean free path is proportional to absolute temperature. II. At constant pressure, mean free time is proportional to the square root of absolute temperature. III. The diatomic gas has molar internal energy $5RT/2$. IV. At fixed number density, pressure is proportional to rms speed.

verdicts.working: At constant pressure, number density is proportional to 1/T, so mean free path ∝ T; mean speed ∝ √T, hence mean free time ∝ √T. A diatomic gas with inactive vibrations has 5 active degrees of freedom, giving Uₘ = 5RT/2. At fixed number density, pressure ∝ vᵣₘₛ², not vᵣₘₛ. Thus I, II, and III are true.

working:
$\lambda=\dfrac{k_BT}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2p}$, so at fixed $p,d$, $\lambda\propto T$. 
$\tau=\lambda/\bar v$ and $\bar v\propto\sqrt{T}$, hence $\tau\propto\sqrt{T}$ at fixed pressure. 
For $f=5$, $U_m=\dfrac{fRT}{2}=\dfrac{5RT}{2}$. 
$p=\dfrac{1}{3}nmv_{\mathrm{rms}}^2$, so IV is false.

Independent check: At constant pressure, number density is proportional to 1/T, so mean free path ∝ T; mean speed ∝ √T, hence mean free time ∝ √T. A diatomic gas with inactive vibrations has 5 active degrees of freedom, giving Uₘ = 5RT/2. At fixed number density, pressure ∝ vᵣₘₛ², not vᵣₘₛ. Thus I, II, and III are true.
solution: For fixed molecular diameter, $\lambda=\dfrac{k_BT}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2p}\propto T$ at constant pressure; since $\bar v\propto\sqrt T$, the mean free time $\tau=\lambda/\bar v\propto\sqrt T$. A diatomic gas with inactive vibrations has $f=5$, so $U_m=\dfrac{fRT}{2}=\dfrac{5RT}{2}$. At fixed number density, $p=\dfrac13nmv_{\rm rms}^2$, so IV is false. Hence I, II and III are true.
